rationale:
Evidence: iteration 4 is the best race so far (score 645.2). It finished 20/20 on the oval (mean 954, 1.99 s), 16/20 on the s-bend (mean 827), and 0/20 on the slalom (progress 0.37, off-track in all 20 runs, 1.0 line-loss event per run). Off-track is still the only end condition on the slalom.

What changed across iterations: going from the 0.024 m array (iteration 2, slalom progress 0.15) to the 0.032 m array (iteration 4, slalom progress 0.37) raised slalom progress with kp still in the stable range. Widening the array is working, and the sensors need to see the tape at larger lateral offsets before line loss is triggered. The slalom is still failing, so the trend should continue.

Changes: (1) Sensor x positions widen to -0.036, -0.018, 0, 0.018, 0.036 at y 0.05, keeping the 12 mm footprint. Tape stays visible to about ±0.048 m of offset, which is beyond the ±0.042 m where the slalom currently leaves. (2) Because the signal per metre of offset falls as the array widens, kp rises slightly from 2.6 to 2.9 to keep steering authority about constant. (3) kd rises from 1.2 to 1.3 to add damping against the faster signal changes at the slalom's reversals, keeping kd/kp near 0.45. (4) base_speed drops from 1.2 to 1.15 to give more time to correct on the sharp bends. The oval has about 1 s of margin, so it should still finish. (5) ki stays 0, weights stay (-2..2), and line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: slalom progress should rise above 0.5, and line-loss events should fall below 1 per run. The oval should still finish at about 2.0 to 2.2 s. The s-bend completion rate should hold or improve. Main risk: a wider array may increase oscillation on the oval, so steering_oscillation and line_loss_events on the oval and slalom are the first things to check.
